Text One: Legionnaires’ disease

Legionnaires’ disease is a type of pneumonia caused by one type of Legionella
bacteria. These bacteria are found i all amounts in bodies of water such as
rivers and lakes in the natural aghonmert. People catch Legionnaires’ disease by
breathing in the bacteria carried in water vapour in the air not by drinking
contaminated water or being exposed to someone with Legionnaires’. The
symptoms of Legionnaires’ disease are similar-to those of the flu including
headache, fever,muscle aches, and respiratory distress. However, more serious
symptoms include mental-confusion and even kidney failure. The disease can be
treated with antibiotics, but is considered to be a life-threatening disease.

Legionnaires’ disease is not common and not everyone who is exposed to the
bacteria will become sick. However, this disease got a lot of publicity in the 1970s,
when it was recognised that the bacteria was growing in air conditioning systems
that use water for heating and cooling. These systems provide an ideal
environment for the bacteria resulting in higher concentrations than in the natural
environment. Buildings also provide continuous exposure which results in a higher
rate of illness. When the source of the disease is the air conditioning system of a
large building, many people may become ill at the same time. The fatality rate of
outbreaks of Legionnaires’ disease ranges from 5 to 50%. :

Individuals whose immune system is under stress for any reason are more
susceptible to this disease. Risk factors include diabetes, pulmonary, heart or
kidney disease, age, smoking, and heavy drinking. Males are also more at risk than

females.

Although air conditioning makes working environments more comfortable, air
conditioning can be(hazardous to health. Although the design of modern air
conditioning systems can reduce the danger of Legionnaires’ disease, this dangerous
respiratory illness is still a risk in older buildings especially in the developing world.
In addition, the warm, humid conditions within an evaporative system can be breeding
grounds for other/bacteria and fungi. In ‘acl 10% af workers in air conditioned have
antibodies which indicate exposure to bacteria growing inside the conditioning
system.

Peni dangers include the recirculation of cigarette smoke. According to an
Australian study which was conducted’before smoking was banned in most public

“puildings; non-smokers could passively “smoke” the equivalent of three cigarettes

during a typical working day merely by breathing the contaminated air within the
building.

To reduce contaminants, many systems use electrostatic precipitators to clean the
circulated air. However, this process results‘in a high level of po: sitive ions in the air,
which causes many building occupants to experience fatigue, irritation and/or

headaches.

Text Four: First Outbreak of Legionnaires’ disease, Philadelphia, US. 1976

On 27 July 1976, members of a U.S. veterans’ group called the American Legion met at the
Bellevue Stratford Hotel in Philadelphia to celebrate the 200" anniversary of the founding of
the United States of America. Within two days, veterans began complaining of chest pain
and breathing difficulties. Over 200 required medical treatment and 34 died.

At first, medical authorities suspected an outbreak of swine flu for which they.had already
been preparing. When this was ruled out, a full medical investigation was carried out. Some
people suspected)that this outbreak was the result of terrorism and they tested for chemical
and biological toxins.

After many months, the authorities began to investigate the environment of the hotel itself.
Finally in January of 1977, the cause was-found in the air conditioning system of the hotel.
This system had provided the ideal breeding ground for the bacterial cause, which was then
named legionella. The bacteria were ther pumped through the entire building setting the
stage for the eventual outbreak of the disease. The severity of this outbreak may be
explained by the health condition of the members of the American Legion, many of whom
would have had several of the risk factors for contracting Legionnaires’ disease.
